cards.text: The LORD is still talking with Moses, Israel's leader, about the tabernacle (Exodus 25-27). Now He turns from the tent to people. He tells Moses to have his brother Aaron brought to him from among the Israelites, along with Aaron's sons Nadab, Abihu, Eleazar and Ithamar.

cards.question: Aaron and his four sons are brought to Moses to serve God as ___.

cards.text: Then God puts in a wardrobe order. He tells Moses to make holy garments for his brother Aaron.

cards.question: God tells Moses to make holy garments for Aaron. What are they meant to give him?
Moses isn't sewing these himself. Who does God tell him to instruct to make Aaron's garments?

cards.text: And God says He's the One who filled those craftsmen with a spirit of wisdom. Their skill came from God, friend, and mine came from burning a WHOLE batch in this bakery and pretending it was on purpose.
God lists the garments: a breastpiece, an ephod, a robe, a woven tunic, a turban and a sash. SIX pieces? That's not an outfit, friend, that's a whole closet.

cards.question: God says these holy garments are just for Aaron and nobody else.

cards.text: They'll use gold, fine linen and blue, purple and scarlet yarn, and the ephod comes first, with two shoulder pieces and a woven waistband made all in one piece. That's ONE piece, friend, with no shortcuts and no 'eh, close enough.'

Then God tells Moses to take two onyx stones and engrave on them the names of the sons of Israel, the man God renamed from Jacob (Genesis 32:28). Six names go on each stone, in the order of their birth.
The names go on the way a gem cutter engraves a seal, and the stones get mounted in gold filigree. As a stamper whose stamps came out blurry for years, I'm a LITTLE jealous.

cards.question: God says Aaron carries the names of the sons of Israel on his two shoulders as a ___ before the LORD.

cards.text: Then come gold filigree settings and two chains of pure gold, braided like cord and attached to the settings. You know when a phone charger comes out of a bag in one big knot? Somebody looked at GOLD and said, 'Let's braid it.'
Next up, the breastpiece of judgment. Sounds serious, friend, and it is.

It's made like the ephod, with gold, colored yarn and fine linen, and it's square when folded double, a span long and a span wide. Then come four rows of gemstones set in gold, from a ruby, a topaz and an emerald in the first row to a beryl, an onyx and a jasper in the fourth. TWELVE gemstones, friend, and I'd be too scared to sneeze anywhere near it.

cards.question: There are twelve stones on the breastpiece. What's engraved on each one?

cards.text: Then come braided chains of pure gold, gold rings at the corners, and a cord of blue yarn tying the breastpiece to the ephod so it doesn't swing out. God thought of EVERYTHING, friend, even the wobble.
Now here's the part I love. In the Holy Place, Aaron carries the names of the sons of Israel on that breastpiece.

cards.question: Aaron wears the breastpiece in the Holy Place. Where on him are the names of the sons of Israel?
The names on the breastpiece are a reminder before the LORD only on Aaron's first day as priest.

cards.text: And God tells Moses to put the Urim and Thummim in the breastpiece too, so they'll also be over Aaron's heart whenever he comes before the LORD.
God says Aaron will continually carry the judgment of the sons of Israel over his heart before the LORD. Not tucked in a back pocket, friend. Right up CLOSE.

Next is the robe of the ephod, entirely blue cloth, with a woven collar around the opening at the top so it won't tear. Everybody who's ever heard that little RRRIP pulling a shirt over their head just stood up and clapped.

Around the lower hem go pomegranates made of blue, purple and scarlet yarn, with gold bells between them, taking turns all the way around. My Ruby, one of my cookie cutter kids, is shaped like a bell, and she'd call that hem her BACKUP CHOIR.
And God says Aaron must wear this robe whenever he ministers.

cards.question: God says the sound of Aaron's robe will be heard when he enters or exits the sanctuary before the LORD. What reason does God give?

answers.text: So that he will not die
So the people will bow down
So the elders will gather near

cards.text: Then God tells Moses to make a plate of pure gold and engrave words on it like a seal.

cards.question: What gets engraved on the gold plate?

cards.text: A blue cord fastens that gold plate to the front of Aaron's turban, and it's to be on his forehead always. God says it's so Aaron may bear the iniquity of the holy things the Israelites consecrate with regard to all their holy gifts.

cards.question: Aaron bears the iniquity of the Israelites' holy gifts with that gold plate on his forehead. What does God say it's for?

answers.text: So they may be acceptable before the LORD
So Aaron may rule over all the tribes
So the people may never sin again

cards.text: Aaron gets a fine linen tunic, a fine linen turban and an embroidered sash, and his sons get tunics, sashes and headbands. The whole family's coordinated, friend, and you KNOW how hard it is to get two people to match for one family photo.

cards.question: God says only Aaron's garments, and not his sons', are meant to give glory and splendor.
Once the garments are on Aaron and his sons, God tells Moses to anoint them, ordain them and consecrate them.

cards.text: Last come linen undergarments, from waist to thigh. Aaron and his sons must wear them whenever they enter the Tent of Meeting or approach the altar, so that they will not incur guilt and die.

cards.question: God gives a rule for Aaron and his sons about wearing linen undergarments whenever they minister. He says it's to be a ___ statute for Aaron and his descendants.

cards.text: That's every last stitch of Aaron's outfit. But hold on to your apron, friend, because God's not done talking to Moses yet.
